title: 27th Sitting of third session of 2025
summary: The 27th sitting of the third session of 2025 met on 1 December 2025 from 09:01 to 11:15, with a recess from 10:31 to 11:00. The Speaker announced a committee seat change, committee meeting notices and a Judicial Service Commission request on removing a judge, which was sent to the Judiciary Committee. Members debated an MDP resolution on unequal treatment in the justice system, which was then voted down, and the chamber heard committee reports on environmental fines, a rules change on petitions, and two finance-related bills, all of which passed. The text layer is partly garbled, so speaker summaries are approximate.

items.title: Resolution by Meekail Ahmed Nasym on discrimination among citizens in the exercise of the power to establish justice
Environment and Climate Change Committee report on fines imposed on parties for harm to the environment

items.title: Closing and next sitting

speakers.name: Mauroof Zakir
positions: Backed the resolution, saying unequal justice erodes public trust, and urged the President to seek a change to the Judicial Service Commission's makeup.
On the petition rules, asked whether the aim is to limit petitions and argued thresholds should reflect the size of each group.
On former Presidents' benefits, said large payouts are hard to justify while basic services and stipends for students abroad lag.

speakers.name: Mohamed Mamdooh
positions: Presented the Environment Committee report on environmental fines, noting large fines for boats hitting reefs and some unpaid or repeated cases.
Presented the Finance Committee report on the Fiscal Responsibility Act amendment, which extends deadlines for the first fiscal charter and regulations.
Presented the Finance Committee report on former Presidents' benefits, saying the committee changes save over MVR 10 million.

speakers.name: Mohamed Ibrahim
positions: Backed the resolution, saying government influence over the courts is visible and citing removals of Supreme Court judges.
On the petition rules, said the signature thresholds would make it harder for small islands to submit petitions.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Didi
positions: Opposed the resolution, saying earlier MDP governments also pressured courts and left court problems unresolved.
Presented the General Committee report adding electronic petitions, saying all committee members agreed on it.

speakers.name: Meekail Ahmed Nasym
positions: Said the resolution only seeks the Majlis's view on unequal treatment, citing short detention for small debts against slow cases involving large sums.
Replied to critics, saying the debate drifted to the proposer instead of the issue, and urged the Majlis to act.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Falah
positions: Raised a point of order over remarks about the President and a member; the Speaker ruled the matter did not qualify as one.
Supported the committee report on former Presidents' and vice presidents' benefits, noting the opposition also backed the changes.

speakers.name: Mohamed Abbas
positions: Argued the resolution is not a fix for unequal justice, saying the poor have long faced harsher treatment in court than the wealthy.

speakers.name: Hussain Shareef
positions: Defended the independence of the justice system and police powers with traffic-fine and vehicle-import examples, and questioned the resolution's premise.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Hussain
positions: Said the resolution is vaguely worded and that the government is working to speed up court cases, including slow loan-recovery cases.

speakers.name: Hussain Ziyad
positions: Backed the resolution, citing a case where a major drug suspect left after a small fee, and called for changing the Judicial Service Commission's makeup.

speakers.name: Hassan Mufeed Abdul Gadir
positions: Said he saw little to support in the resolution but wanted his view recorded, and noted the promise to change the Judicial Service Commission was unmet.

decisions: Mohamed Ali (Dhuvaafaru) joined the Social Committee in place of Asma Rasheed as the PNC representative.
The Judicial Service Commission's request on removing a judge was sent to the Judiciary Committee for study.
A proposal to amend the Majlis rules (Rules 23 and 30) was sent to the General Committee.
The resolution on discrimination in the justice system was not carried (10 yes, 56 no).
The Environment and Climate Change Committee report on environmental fines was passed (67-0).
The amendment to Chapter 51 of the Majlis rules on petitions was passed (57-9).
The bill amending the Fiscal Responsibility Act (Law 2024/30) was passed (58-9).
The bill amending the law on benefits for former Presidents (Law 2009/9) was passed (68-0).
The next sitting was set for 3 December 2025 at 09:00.

votes.what: Resolution by Meekail Ahmed Nasym on discrimination in the exercise of the power to establish justice (not carried)
Environment and Climate Change Committee report on fines imposed for environmental harm
General Committee report on amending Chapter 51 (petitions) of the Majlis rules
Bill amending the Fiscal Responsibility Act (Law 2024/30), Finance Committee report
Bill amending the law on protection and benefits for former Presidents (Law 2009/9), Finance Committee report
